newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent trades weaker, supply seen plentiful.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent trades weaker, supply seen plentiful.

text.p: Dated Brent crude oil traded two cents weaker on Tuesday and looked set for further falls amid ample prompt North Sea supply and pressure from unsold West African barrels, traders said.
A Wall Street refiner sold a March 24-26 cargo for April Brent less 37 cents a barrel, after active trade on Monday at April less 35 cents.
Another four Brents were available, in addition to the three turning wet, and traders expected the next deal to be weaker.
Other North Sea grades were also suffering from the overhang of unsold March barrels, traders said.
Gullfaks A loading at the end of the month was sold for Dated Brent less 47 cents a barrel, compared to Friday's deal on a March 17-19 cargo at Dated Brent less 15 cents.
Traders said there was more Gullfaks available in addition to five or six unsold Osebergs and a handful of Ekofisks.
"The picture is awful, particularly for Gullfaks which is a gas oil grade," said a trader.
"And there's too much West African around," he added.
Early April Bonny Light fetched Dated Brent plus 19 cents on Tuesday, 39 cents below the March Official Selling Price, as a surplus of March cargoes began to feed through into next month.
The only North Sea loading programme released so far on Tuesday showed Flotta volumes rising about 17,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 6.35 million barrels in April.
Brent paper markets reflected the sloppy physical sentiment, with April/May trading at +5 cents. May/June was talked at evens/+5 after trade on Monday at +4 cents.
Next week's CFDs also appeared to lose ground, amid talk of an afternoon deal at May Brent -25 cents after trade earlier at May Brent -21 cents, dealers said.
